Adam Fox has 22 points in 20 games, 20 of them assists, and the uncomfortable part for the rest of the league is that the number could be bigger. With Fox on the ice at five-on-five, the Rangers take 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 8.7 points better than when he sits. Yet New York has scored 6.6 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him out there. That kind of shortfall usually swings back, which is why our flag on him reads "due" even though his scoring already runs ahead of our talent range.

The Rangers have leaned on him harder lately: 24.2 minutes a night over his last ten, up almost three from his norm, with 13 points in that stretch. The New York Times put it bluntly in a headline this week: "If you don’t think Adam Fox is one of the NHL’s best defensemen, you’re not paying attention." The 2021 Norris winner was worth 2.9 wins above replacement last season by Evolving-Hockey's count, ninth among 215 defensemen, most of it on defense. He isn't a shooter (28 shots, two goals). He's the reason everyone else gets to shoot.
headline: Adam Fox is driving play and getting shorted
